paper_title: The Canadian Traveller Problem on Outerplanar Graphs
classifications: Theory of computation → Graph algorithms analysis
statement: To achieve constant competitive ratio on arbitrarily weighted graphs, a good √ candidate could be graphs with bounded-sized minimal edge (s, t)-cuts, for which ratio 2k + O(1) is known [12]. Observe that our construction T which disproves constant ratio increases the size of edge (s, t)-cuts. We conjecture that there exists a polynomial-time deterministic strategy achieving constant competitive ratio on graphs with edge (s, t)-cuts of bounded size.
context: Since some sub-families of outerplanar graphs have constant competitive ratio in the weighted case (trees and cycles, which imply cacti from Lemma 2.2) while a very close superfamily admits the general bound 2k + 1 in the unit-weighted case (planar of treewidth 2), a natural question is to investigate where the competitive gaps lie in both cases. For the unit-weighted case, future research could focus on the natural extension of p-outerplanar graphs [4], with p successive outer faces, in order to generalize constant competitiveness.
